paper.citation: Vázquez-Villarreal LG, Carvajal-Veitía W, Guevara-Balcázar G, Maceroni C, López-Sánchez P, Castillo-Hernández MC. Position-Specific Kinanthropometric Traits of Professional American Football Players: A Study of Mexican LFA Players. J Funct Morphol Kinesiol. 2026;11:109.
paper.abstract: This cross-sectional study profiled 189 professional players from seven positions in the 2019-2020 Mexican LFA seasons using ISAK anthropometry, five-component body composition fractionation, somatotype and proportionality indices. Offensive and defensive linemen were the largest players with the highest adipose, muscle and bone masses, while defensive backs and wide receivers had lower endomorphy.
paper.tldr: A position-by-position anthropometric reference for 189 Mexican LFA players, showing linemen are the largest and skill-position players the leanest. It is descriptive context for positional profiling, not a predictor of performance.
paper.methods: Cross-sectional observational study following STROBE guidance, with 189 players across seven positions measured by ISAK Level 3 anthropometrists using 26 variables. Body composition used the Ross and Kerr fractionation method and somatotype used the Heath-Carter method, with ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis tests and an exploratory stepwise discriminant analysis.
paper.findings: Linemen had the greatest body mass, adiposity and muscle mass, and the overall somatotype was an endomorphic mesomorph (3.8-7.0-0.8). The exploratory discriminant model, using arm relaxed girth, biiliocristal breadth and sitting height, classified 57.7% of players correctly (offensive linemen 85.7%, running backs 37.5%) and was not cross-validated.
paper.limitations: The sample comes from a single league and excludes kickers, and body composition was estimated by anthropometric fractionation rather than DXA or air-displacement plethysmography. The design is cross-sectional with no longitudinal data, measurements were taken before the COVID-19 disruption, and the discriminant model is exploratory and not cross-validated.
paper.practicalImplications: ISAK-based position reference values can help staff compare a player with a league-specific positional profile. The authors present these values as descriptive and do not link them to on-field performance.
paper.athleteDev: Provides a Mexican LFA position-specific anthropometric reference (body mass, girths, skinfolds, somatotype, proportionality) that may support morphological profiling and talent identification. The discriminant model (57.7% accuracy, exploratory) should not be used to classify individual players.
paper.rtp: Not applicable: the study describes body morphology in healthy professional players and does not assess injury, rehabilitation or return to sport, so it cannot inform return-to-sport decisions.
